note: The core subset -- the port surface a second host must implement to run grammar/interp.planes. Declared here as a single source of truth (as grammar/vocabulary.json is for the full surface) and enforced by core_check.py, which fails when interp.planes uses any keyword or builtin outside it. Derived from evidence: every member is a construct interp.planes actually uses; every excluded construct is one it provably avoids. CORE_SUBSET.md is the prose derivation; this file is what the checker reads. Effect kinds are NOT listed as constraints -- all seven are core (an interpreter performs whatever it interprets, confirmed by shapes in Phase 5), so they are never flagged.

excluded_keywords.let: plain `=` suffices everywhere; interp.planes never writes `let`
excluded_keywords.rule: a rule is a checker constraint, not an interpreter action
excluded_keywords.when: dispatch is flat `if k == ...` on the node kind (A.1/A.6), never `when subject is {...}` -- so `when` is NOT needed, refuting CORE_SUBSET.md's claim that it is the only substitute for the absent isinstance
excluded_keywords.why: provenance query is a tool, not a language the interpreter needs; the deriv slot stays nothing (A.6)

size.builtins: 11 of 12 -- interp.planes delegates every ordinary builtin to the host, `number` (A-Q19) among them; `sine` is the one exception, reimplemented from exact parts rather than called, because showing that derivation was the point of adding it
